text.tspan: # unit tests: bcrypt ($2b$ from Python), JWT, json.dumps, isoformat, fallback maths

g.text: python backend-rs/tests/compare/compare.py # Python vs Rust on one Postgres, every endpoint
On a Windows box without MSVC/MinGW use zig as the C toolchain: pip install ziglang cargo-zigbuild,
put a dlltool.exe shim that runs zig dlltool on PATH (windows-gnu needs one for raw-dylib), then cargo
zigbuild. Gotchas hit while doing that: sqlx's chrono feature produced binaries that segfault before main with
that linker (hence the time crate here), and the embedded Postgres from pgserver ships without tz data, so
sqlx's SET TimeZone='UTC' fails until a share/postgresql/timezone directory (e.g. from the tzdata
wheel) is added. Neither affects Linux/Docker builds.
The harness sets the test database to timezone = 'UTC', like the postgres Docker image.
Python stores tz-aware datetimes into timestamp columns through the session TimeZone, Rust always writes
UTC; if production Postgres runs in another TimeZone the two would disagree.
compare.py points both backends at a mock Anthropic server through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
(honoured by the Python SDK and by this crate).
compare.py masks ids/tokens/timestamps, compares status, JSON body and key order, cross-checks bcrypt
hashes and JWTs in both directions, and compares cv_data.extracted_text (PyPDF2 vs the Rust extractor)
